sentences.text: The assessment was conducted with **Margaret Doyle** (S2) in her own home, where the social worker Priya Nair (S1) entered via the front door.
The referral for this assessment was made by the hospital upon Margaret Doyle’s discharge.
The assessment is conducted under the **Care Act** to understand Margaret Doyle’s daily living, challenges, and what matters most to her.
The assessment aims to determine if support is needed and whether Margaret Doyle is eligible for **council-funded care support**.

Margaret Doyle has experienced **three falls in the last six months**, including a fall on **March 3rd** (Monday) in the kitchen while feeling dizzy or woozy, likely due to a lack of food. She was unable to get up immediately due to wrist pain and was found two hours later by Brenda next door.

She was diagnosed with a **fractured left wrist** (left-handed) and has bruising on her right side (left side of her body). Her wrist was in a splint after the cast came off on **Tuesday 17th March**, but she does not consistently follow the required exercises.
Margaret Doyle uses a **walker indoors** but sometimes holds onto furniture instead, and it frequently gets caught on rugs or doorframes, making mobility difficult.
She struggles with **stairs**—using a rail on the right side while ascending but descending sideways or sitting down due to rail placement. She holds onto the wall for support upstairs.
She avoids drinking in the afternoon to reduce bathroom trips, which may contribute to dehydration and dizziness. She has not bathed since January due to fear of falling while getting out.

She has **not used a bath lift or assistive device** since January and struggles with washing and dressing, particularly buttons, bra hooks, and laces. Dressing takes **40–60 minutes**, leaving her exhausted.
Margaret Doyle uses **pads at night**, bought by Kevin, and is interested in the **free continence service** for advice and free pads.

Her **daily eating routine** includes toast with marmalade, tin soup, and yoghurt with crackers, but she has stopped cooking due to fear of falling in the kitchen. She lost nearly a stone (180g) since Christmas and has a fluctuating appetite.

She takes **amlodipine (5mg daily)**, **alendronic acid (70mg weekly)**, and **paracetamol (up to 4x daily)** for wrist pain. She has missed some medication (amlodipine twice last week) and occasionally forgets her tablets.
Margaret Doyle explicitly stated she **does not want to be placed in a care facility** and wants to remain in her own home.
She prefers to stay in her own home and has **denied any interest in sheltered flats or bungalows with a warden**, citing sentimental value.
She mentioned **Beechwood home** as a future preference if she ever needed care.
Margaret Doyle’s son, Kevin Doyle, supports her preference for her home but expresses concerns about her safety.
Margaret Doyle values her **roses and wants to see them thrive this summer**, intending to go out and admire them.
She wants a **proper bath** and the ability to wash her hair regularly.
Margaret Doyle misses attending the **St Michael’s lunch club** (now on Thursdays) and enjoys the activities, including recent owl presentations.
She misses socializing with **Joan and Pat** and feels **lonely**, especially on days when no one visits. She watches TV and does word searches to cope.
She has **not had thoughts of self-harm or suicide** but would tell Dr Shah or Susan if her mood worsened.
Margaret Doyle loves her grandson Jordan but worries about his **financial decisions, particularly potential gambling** via betting apps.

Margaret Doyle disclosed **unauthorized withdrawals of approximately £600 over two months** from her bank account, likely by her grandson Jordan. She gave her PIN to Jordan when she was out of hospital.
Margaret Doyle **denied knowing if Jordan had access to her PIN** but confirmed he used her card for withdrawals and groceries.
Kevin Doyle heard from Brenda that he saw Jordan using Margaret’s card at a cash machine on the high street.
Margaret Doyle **explicitly stated she does not want the police involved** and requested her bank card be canceled and a new one issued with a new PIN.
Kevin Doyle suggested ringing the police but Margaret Doyle requested the safeguarding team be informed.
Margaret Doyle’s concern about Jordan’s potential **gambling** was noted as **hearsay** (not confirmed).
Margaret Doyle’s **financial situation** includes a £9,000 savings account (funeral money and small amount for grandchildren) and a state pension plus widow’s pension.
She has not previously been informed about **Attendance Allowance** and would need help filling out the form due to difficulty with her hand.

Margaret Doyle’s **support network** includes her son, Kevin Doyle (who shops and reminds her about medication), her daughter, Brenda (who provides milk and bread), and her grandson, Jordan (who occasionally visits).
Kevin Doyle has discussed **removing loose rugs** in the house since 2010 but Margaret Doyle **did not want to discuss this further with the social worker**.
Margaret Doyle’s **financial situation** includes a state pension, widow’s pension, and savings of £9,000. She has missed some of her medication and is short on money recently.
She is unsure if she is eligible for **Attendance Allowance** and would prefer to pay a small amount toward care costs if necessary to stay in her own home.
Kevin Doyle will assist Margaret Doyle with **canceling her bank card and ordering a new one with a new PIN** on Friday morning.
The social worker (Priya Nair) will **refer Margaret Doyle to the safeguarding adults team** regarding the unauthorized card usage.
Margaret Doyle will be sent the **Attendance Allowance form** and offered help with filling it out by Kevin Doyle.
The social worker will explore **medication reminders** (alarm or carer visit) with Margaret Doyle.
The social worker will revisit **financial matters** with Margaret Doyle at a later stage.

Margaret Doyle will be referred to **occupational therapy (OT)** for a bath lift, a second stair rail, a second frame upstairs, and a review of the back step and pull cord. The waiting list is approximately three weeks, but the referral is marked as a priority.
The social worker will refer Margaret Doyle to the **continence service** if she agrees, providing free pads and advice.

The social worker will ensure no **bossy carers** are assigned and will explore Margaret Doyle’s concerns about daily visits for washing, dressing, medication, and meal preparation for six weeks at no cost.
Kevin Doyle will ask about the **support Margaret will receive** after the assessment.
